title: The State of Kernel Self Protection Project by Kees Cook, Google
summary: Kees Cook of Google gives a Linux Foundation talk on the Kernel Self Protection Project, which aims to harden Linux against attackers. He surveys threats, the state of available defensive technologies and a year of community progress.
why: Cited as the authoritative overview of kernel hardening goals and priorities, including Cook's car-safety analogy for kernel security.

quote.text: I really enjoyed this talk about KSPP's agenda
